findings.description: Define identifies work already covered by an existing change but does not explicitly stop duplicate creation.
findings.analysis: The revised workflow asks the agent to check whether existing work already covers the request, but only directs it to explain a boundary. A fully covered request has no meaningful boundary and could still produce a duplicate defined change.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly report the existing evidence and stop without creating a change when the request is already covered; retain boundary explanation for partial overlap.
findings.rationale: Fully covered requests should not create duplicate changes; partial overlap remains visible through an explicit boundary.

findings.description: Definition and activation need explicit user-alignment summaries before their respective boundaries.
findings.analysis: A substantive definition should be confirmed before it becomes a durable queued change. Likewise, estimates, design, and tasks should be confirmed together before activation commences build, even with decision-gated progression enabled.
findings.recommendation: Add a definition-confirmation summary before finalising a defined record and an activation-readiness summary plus explicit build confirmation after preparation completes.
findings.rationale: Superseded by the user's clarification: define presents a summary but never requires confirmation; only starting build requires explicit confirmation.

findings.description: Only build start is a confirmation boundary; define presents its summary without gating and tasks does not pause.
findings.analysis: A defined change remains independent queued work, so confirmation is unnecessary. The material decision occurs immediately before implementation begins, regardless of which planning stages have run.
findings.recommendation: Remove definition and tasks confirmation gates, present a non-blocking define summary, and make build require explicit confirmation before it changes implementation.
findings.rationale: User explicitly clarified the intended boundary.

findings.description: Human-facing lifecycle documentation and define lifecycle guidance do not describe the new confirmation boundaries.
findings.analysis: The changed skills require confirmation before durable definition and build, but the human lifecycle reference and define row do not yet say so.
findings.recommendation: Add concise confirmation-boundary language to the lifecycle reference and package policy.
findings.rationale: Document that define presents a summary, but do not describe it as a confirmation boundary. Document the sole confirmation boundary before build.

findings.description: Tasks has no durable signal that activation invoked it as a preparation-chain stage.
findings.analysis: The new exception relies on an agent inferring call context. A mistaken inference can let decision-gated progression invoke build directly and bypass the readiness confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Define an explicit, checkable activation-chain signal or a durable state-based condition.
findings.rationale: Tasks must not infer activation context or pause. Replace the task exception with a direct build-start confirmation guard that applies regardless of preceding planning stages.

findings.description: Decision-gated policy does not list definition or build-readiness confirmations as mandatory stops.
findings.analysis: The automation policy's stop list omits the two new user decisions, while lifecycle and skill guidance require them. Reading the automation policy alone can suggest automatic progression is allowed.
findings.recommendation: Add both confirmation boundaries to the mandatory-stop list.
findings.rationale: Decision-gated workflow policy must explicitly stop before build for the alignment summary and user confirmation.

findings.description: Build must restate the change specification before requesting confirmation to commence implementation.
findings.analysis: The start-of-build decision consumes implementation time and tokens, so the user needs a concise current statement of the intended work at that point.
findings.recommendation: Require build to present an alignment summary derived from the change specification and wait for explicit confirmation before the first implementation action.
findings.rationale: User explicitly requires a specification restatement at the sole confirmation boundary.

findings.description: Define does not say how to handle a slug collision discovered after the user confirms the definition summary.
findings.analysis: The workflow chooses and checks the slug only after user confirmation, so a collision needs an explicit deterministic response.
findings.recommendation: Select and validate a unique slug before presenting it, or choose an adjusted unique slug after confirmation and report it.
findings.rationale: A duplicate slug is blocking. Report the conflicting change and let the user choose a new name or investigate whether the same-name change already covers the work.

findings.description: Activate mixes US and UK/AU spelling for artefact, and the supplied review JSON remains untracked.
findings.analysis: The project requires UK/AU English for human-facing guidance. The untracked report is a user-supplied review source and should remain outside a scoped change commit unless explicitly requested.
findings.recommendation: Use artefact consistently in activate guidance; leave the supplied review source uncommitted.
findings.rationale: Review-source files remain excluded from change scope. Correct the one inconsistent use of `artefact` to the accepted software-industry spelling `artifact`.
